harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Node1 now publishes the approved boot tree as a persistent, read-only TFTP root. Node2 successfully downloads boot.cfg and firmware.bin with byte-identical hashes. Uploads, overwrites, and requests outside the boot root are rejected. Both nodes retained RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 and passed sequential restart/recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL 9 repository-supported tftp-server on node1 and tftp client on node2.
Configured /srv/legacy2/tftp-firmware-distribution/boot as the secure TFTP root.
Applied root ownership, read-only file permissions, persistent SELinux labels, firewalld configuration, and socket activation.
Configured node2's persistent TFTP conntrack helper for negotiated UDP transfers.
Verified downloads, hashes, upload rejection, overwrite rejection, and path-traversal rejection.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Publish boot.cfg and firmware.bin from node1 with preserved bytes
evidence.summary: Node2 downloaded both files; downloaded SHA-256 hashes match node1's sources. The final server check shows the intended secure root, active UDP/69 listener, SELinux labels, and read-only modes.

evidence.requirement: Reject uploads and requests outside the boot root
evidence.summary: New uploads, overwrite attempts, and ../private traversal returned TFTP errors before and after restarts. Unauthorized targets remain absent and approved file hashes are unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8. TFTP packages came from the configured RHEL 9 repositories.

Healthy baseline captured; safe reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 377b5195-7fea-4219-a67b-044ef3f7ab99 to 2c970bef-d6df-42b7-8db5-1ecaa14458c7. TFTP, firewall access, file metadata, hashes, and node2 downloads recovered.

Healthy baseline captured; safe reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 3aee314b-4dfc-4c3a-90f6-2b07c621eaa0 to 399993f6-1421-416d-8ec6-cb4e7765fb04. The firewall helper recovered and both TFTP downloads again matched source hashes.
